entries.label: Gotcha
entries.prompt: Ultra-detailed macro product photograph of a single real fly-fishing fly on a seamless pure white background, studio softbox lighting, sharp focus, side profile view, no hands, no text. The fly is a "Gotcha". Standard-length stainless saltwater hook, size 4. Construction from the eye back: a prominent, glossy, built-up pale-pink thread head at the very front; then a pair of silver BEAD-CHAIN EYES: exactly TWO small polished steel balls, each about the size of the hook eye, joined by a hidden stub of two or three tiny chain links, the whole piece lashed CROSSWISE over the shank with figure-eight thread wraps so that one ball sits out to the left of the shank and one to the right, like a tiny barbell. Seen from the side one ball is in front and the other directly behind it, both level with the shank. There is NO loose chain anywhere — no chain wrapped around the body, no chain hanging below, no chain showing between the balls, set about two hook-eye widths back from the hook eye; behind the eyes a sparse tan craft-fur wing tied on the hook-point side of the shank, one and a half to two shank lengths long and sweeping well past the bend, with three or four strands of pearl Krystal Flash through it; a body of flat pearl Diamond Braid wrapped in overlapping turns along the shank and figure-eighted around the eyes; and at the bend a tail of the same pearl braid, shredded and picked out into a fan about one shank length past the bend. The craft-fur wing and the hook point are on the SAME side of the shank and the fly fishes upside down: show the hook point facing UP with the tan wing directly above the shank on the same side as the point, screening the point, the pearl braid body below, and the two bead-chain balls straddling the shank just behind the pink head. INVERTED — CHECK THIS: in the finished image the hook point must appear ABOVE the shank, aimed toward the TOP of the frame, with the hook gap opening upward and the bend curving up. The bead-chain eyes straddle the shank at shank height — one ball each side — they do not hang below it. Do not render this fly point-down. FRAMING: strict side profile with the hook EYE at the LEFT of the frame and the hook BEND and tail to the RIGHT. The fly is rendered LARGE in the frame: the whole fly including the entire hook fills the frame from side to side, its length spanning about 80% of the image width with only a narrow even margin around it. Do NOT render a small fly floating in a large empty frame — fill the frame regardless of how small the real fly is. Sharp focus front to back. Exactly ONE fly in the image — one single complete fly, not two flies side by side, not a pair, not a row, not a size range. No hands, no vise, no tools, no water, no packaging, no text, no watermark, no border.

A freshwater scud (Amphipoda, e.g. Gammarus), side view, aquatic, body curled into a comma or C shape. Body about 12 mm long, strongly flattened side to side so it is tall and narrow, divided into roughly thirteen visible segments with no shell-like carapace over the back. Small head with two pairs of antennae, the second pair long and whip-like, and small black sessile compound eyes set flush in the head with no eyestalks. Two pairs of small clawed grasping gnathopods at the front, followed by seven pairs of slender jointed walking legs along the thorax, then several pairs of short feathery swimming pleopods beneath the curled abdomen and three small pairs of uropods at the tail end, with no flat fan tail. Translucent olive to tan with faint darker banding and a hint of orange. It is a live freshwater crustacean, an amphipod, not an insect, not a true shrimp, and not a shrimp cocktail.

entries.label: Aquatic worm — adult
entries.prompt: Scientific natural-history illustration, ink line and soft watercolor wash on plain cream paper, accurate anatomy, no text, no labels. An aquatic worm, a single live animal in side view lying in a loose relaxed curve on a silty bottom, about 3 cm long. A very simple animal: a thin, soft, smooth, evenly segmented cylindrical body with fine close-set rings along its whole length, tapering gently at both ends, translucent wine-red to pink with a paler underside and a faint darker line of the gut showing through. It has NO legs, NO head capsule, NO eyes, NO antennae, NO bristles, NO tails, NO wings and no hard parts anywhere — nothing but the soft segmented tube. It is an annelid worm, not an insect larva, not a midge larva, not a leech, and not a fly-tying pattern.

entries.label: Sculpin — adult
entries.prompt: Scientific entomological illustration, ink line and soft watercolor wash on plain cream paper, accurate anatomy, no text, no labels. A sculpin (Cottidae, e.g. Cottus bairdii), a small bottom-dwelling fish about 8 cm long, side view resting on gravel underwater. Broad flattened wedge-shaped head, wider than the body, with a wide mouth and eyes set high on top of the head; the head tapers abruptly into a slender tubular body that narrows to the tail. Skin scaleless and slightly velvety. Two dorsal fins along the back - a low soft-spined front fin followed by a longer soft-rayed second fin - a single anal fin below the rear, very large fan-shaped pectoral fins spread wide just behind the head, small pelvic fins beneath them, and a rounded caudal fin. Faint lateral line along the flank. Olive-brown to slate grey, heavily mottled and speckled darker, with about four indistinct dark saddle bars across the back and a pale belly. It is a live freshwater fish, not an insect and not a tadpole.

entries.label: Leech — adult
entries.prompt: Scientific entomological illustration, ink line and soft watercolor wash on plain cream paper, accurate anatomy, no text, no labels. A freshwater leech (Hirudinea), adult, side view swimming in open water, body about 5 cm long in a smooth up-and-down undulating wave. Soft muscular worm-like body, flattened from top to bottom, tapering at both ends, its surface finely ringed by many close-set transverse annuli grouped into about thirty-four body segments. A small narrow sucker at the head end with several tiny paired dark eyespots along the top near the front, and a larger round disc-shaped sucker at the rear end. No legs, no bristles, no antennae. Glossy dark olive-brown to near-black on the back, often with fine paler speckling or a dull orange to olive underside. It is a live aquatic annelid worm, not an insect larva, not an eel, and not a strip of rabbit fur.
